evidence.quote: ואחרים אמרו: כי טעם להזכיר המבול, בעבור שהזכיר חלק מנפלאותיו והוא רדת הגשם, הזכיר הפלא העצום והוא הגשם הרב בימי נח ... ויש אומרים: כי הזכיר המבול – בעבור השבועה שמים לא ישחתו כל הארץ ... ויש אומרים: כי מיום שישב לשפוט בימי המבול נראתה מלכותו

claims.explanation: Ibn Ezra offers explanations for mentioning the Flood, including the oath, but does not recount the kings’ exchange with Balaam.
claims.suggested_fix: Change “(and Rashi and Ibn Ezra on v. 10)” to “(and Rashi on v. 10; Ibn Ezra also mentions the post-Flood oath)”.

claims.sentence: In b. Zevachim 116a:23 (and Rashi and Ibn Ezra on v. 10), when the terrified kings ask Balaam whether a flood is coming (`שֶׁמָּא מַבּוּל בָּא לָעוֹלָם – ה׳ לַמַּבּוּל יָשָׁב`), Balaam answers with v. 10b (`וַיֵּשֶׁב ה׳ מֶלֶךְ לְעוֹלָם`) that God already swore after the Flood never again to bring a flood, quoting Gen 9:15 (`וְלֹא־יִהְיֶה עוֹד הַמַּיִם לְמַבּוּל`) (Rabbinic Reception, Verse 10 — Zevachim 116a:23; Rashi and Ibn Ezra on v. 10).
claims.claim: Balaam explicitly quotes Genesis 9:15

evidence.quote: [אמר להם]: ״וישב ה׳ מלך לעולם״ – כבר נשבע הקדוש ברוך הוא שאינו מביא מבול לעולם.
וְלֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֥ה ע֛וֹד מַבּ֖וּל לְשַׁחֵ֥ת הָאָֽרֶץ׃

claims.explanation: Balaam states the oath but does not quote Genesis 9:15. Genesis 9:11 also states the promise, so the unspecific allusion does not identify 9:15 as its exact cited verse.
claims.suggested_fix: Change “quoting Gen 9:15” to “alluding to the post-Flood promise (cf. Gen 9:11, 15)”.

claims.sentence: Parallel judicial idiom `יָשַׁב לְ־` ("sit for [judgment/governance]", cf. Ps 9:8; 122:5) vs. `עַל־הַמָּיִם` in v. 3 (Verse-Level Notes, v. 10; Figurative Language Insights, Throne #2).
claims.claim: Psalm 9:8 has judicial יָשַׁב לְ־

evidence.quote: וַֽ֭יהֹוָה לְעוֹלָ֣ם יֵשֵׁ֑ב כּוֹנֵ֖ן לַמִּשְׁפָּ֣ט כִּסְאֽוֹ׃
כִּ֤י שָׁ֨מָּה ׀ יָשְׁב֣וּ כִסְא֣וֹת לְמִשְׁפָּ֑ט כִּ֝סְא֗וֹת לְבֵ֣ית דָּוִֽד׃

claims.explanation: Psalm 9:8 says the LORD sits *forever* and establishes a throne *for judgment*; its לְ after the sitting verb is temporal, not “for judgment.” Psalm 122:5 does put sitting thrones and “for judgment” together.
claims.suggested_fix: Change the parenthesis to “cf. Ps 9:8, which links sitting forever with a throne for judgment, and 122:5, where thrones sit for judgment”.

claims.sentence: What looks in b. Zevachim 116a like a homiletical leap—reading "YHWH sat `לַמַּבּוּל`" as a reassurance that no new flood will destroy the world—is actually anchored in a precise lexical *gezerah shavah* between the only two `למבול` forms in Scripture (Ps 29:10 and Gen 9:15), and illuminates the psalm's own logic: the storm over `הַמָּיִם` (v. 3) ends in `שָׁלוֹם` (v. 11) because YHWH's eternal throne at the `מַבּוּל` (v. 10) guarantees that `הַמָּיִם` will never again become `לְמַבּוּל`.
claims.claim: Zevachim derives its reading through lexical gezerah shavah

evidence.quote: שמא מבול בא לעולם (אמר להם) – ״ה׳ למבול ישב״? [אמר להם]: ״וישב ה׳ מלך לעולם״ – כבר נשבע הקדוש ברוך הוא שאינו מביא מבול לעולם.

claims.explanation: The two biblical forms do match, but the Talmud does not cite Genesis 9:15 or present a verbal derivation from that match. The proposed lexical link is the guide’s observation, not an attested *gezerah shavah* in Zevachim.
claims.suggested_fix: Change “is actually anchored in a precise lexical *gezerah shavah* between” to “can be read alongside the precise lexical match between”.

claims.sentence: Commentators note that `מַבּוּל` occurs only in Gen 6–11 and Ps 29:10, without noticing that the prefixed form `למבול` is shared exclusively by Ps 29:10 and the rainbow-covenant oath of Gen 9:15 (`הַמַּיִם לְמַבּוּל`), which is the exact verse b. Zevachim 116a uses to unlock v. 10.
claims.claim: Commentators explicitly note the noun’s exclusive distribution
